sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Low-level design (LLD) interview questions test whether you can take an ambiguous prompt ("design a parking lot", "design a cab-booking system") and produce a clean class diagram in 30 minutes — using OOP correctly, identifying entities and relationships, applying the right design patterns, and writing code that compiles. This page covers the LLD prompts that recur most often, with the classes, the patterns used, and the Java code skeletons.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
LLD = take a fuzzy prompt, produce a **clean class diagram** in 30 minutes:

- **Identify entities** — nouns in the prompt.
- **Define behaviours** — verbs become methods.
- **Apply patterns** — Strategy / State / Factory / Observer where intent matches.
- **Code skeleton** — interfaces first, classes second, tests if time permits.
- **Concurrency** — declare it: which methods are thread-safe and how.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Elevator system** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Encapsulation** — make state private; expose intentionally.
- **Open-closed** — new behaviour by extension, not modification.
- **Avoid premature interfaces** — extract one when you have ≥ 2 implementations.
- **Mutability** — default to immutable; opt into mutability with reason.
- **Don't model the database** — model the domain.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"Entities: <A, B, C>. Relationships: <association / composition>. The behaviour split is <service A vs domain B>; I'd apply <pattern> for <intent>. Concurrency: <which methods need synchronisation> and the data is <immutable / atomic / locked>."*
